Steam release game: "Beware the Sabertooth!"
The players are members of the Crood family / Caveman Tribe.
The leader (or animator) is Grug (or the Tribe Leader), armed
with a loud whistle or horn (the "Warning Horn").Out in the
dangerous prehistoric wild, roaming alone means getting eaten
by a Sabertooth Tiger or a Bear Owl! The only way to survive is
to stick together in Packs.
How to Play
1. Scattered Tribe:
All the cavemen run around the area, making caveman
noises (grunting, beating their chests, acting like
prehistoric animals, or foraging for "food").
2. The Danger Signal:
When the Leader blows the whistle, everyone stops
running and listens carefully. The Leader yells out a
survival rule, such as:
○ "SABERTOOTH ATTACK! PACKS OF 4!"
○ "ROCK SLIDE! GROUPS OF 3!"
○ "NIGHTTIME IS DANGEROUS! CAVEMEN IN
5s!"
3. Form the Pack:
Players must quickly huddle together to form groups of
that exact size. To make it extra thematic, they must link
arms or put their heads together in a "family huddle" and
yell "NEVER NOT BE AFRAID!").
4. Out of the Pack:

Cubs sit in a circle and are numbered one to six. A cell
phone is placed in the centre of the circle.
The leader shares an emergency scenario with the Pack, for
example: “There has been an accident at the public
swimming pool on the corner of Spine and Eisleben in
Mitchells Plain. A young boy has injured his head and is
bleeding.”
The leader then calls out a number. All Cubs with that
number stand up, run clockwise around the outside of the
circle, and return to their place. The first Cub to reach
the telephone pretends to dial the emergency number
and clearly delivers the message.
• If the message is correct, the Cub scores one point.
• If the Cub hesitates or gives incorrect information, the other
Cub(s) with the same number may raise a hand and have a
turn.
• The first Cub to give the correct message earns the point.
Remind Cubs that emergency numbers are for real
emergencies only. Always tell the operator where you are,
what happened, give your contact number, and stay on
the line.

BASE 4: DEMONSTRATION: Recovery position
The first thing to do, without delay, is to lay the victim
on their side, open the airway and keep it open. If the
head is tilted forwards this may obstruct the airway and
hinder breathing, so tilt the person’s head back as far
as it can go. Very often breathing will start again quite
naturally. A person who cannot breathe naturally will
struggle for breath, and their face and lips will turn blue.
As soon as natural breathing starts, the heaving
movements of the chest will stop, and the colour of the
face and lips will turn pink again.

tagging. Tagging doesn’t count if the chain is
broken. The game continues until all the Cubs have
been tagged.

Initial Snares: Select four players (Cubs) to stand at opposite
points along an imaginary circular boundary. Each pair holds
hands high to form a "snare" arch.
The Klipspringers: The rest of the group line up as a herd of
agile klipspringers ready to leap and run around the circle,
passing directly through each snare arch.
The Catch: When the leader blows the whistle, the snares drop
their arms to catch any passing klipspringer.
Expanding the Snares: Any klipspringers caught in the net
must pair up, raise their hands, and form a new snare arch along
the circle.
Odd-Man-Out: If a single klipspringer is caught without a pair,
they wait briefly in the center—the next captured klipspringer will
join them to form the next arch.
Objective: Play continues until all klipspringers have been
caught and converted into snare arches.

records.activity:
The story of Kim
Baden-Powell’s believed that Kim, the main character in a story his friend Rudyard
Kipling wrote, was a good example of what a scout could be. One of Kim’s skills was
that he was incredibly observant. This is Kim’s story.
A long time ago in India there was a boy named Kimball O'Hara, but everyone called
him Kim. He grew up on the streets of Lahore, clever and quick-eyed, always
watching, always learning. One of the things he was called by the locals was, “"Little
friend of all the world.” He was a friend to all, just like a scout (and cub) should be.
One day Kim met a spy trainer called Lurgan Sahib. He trained Kim and his test was
simple: objects on a tray, covered, and you had to remember every single one. Kim
trained and trained until his memory became razor-sharp. He became one of the
greatest secret agents in the land.

to remember it

what they were

all

○ More than 6 correct: 4 marbles

records.activity:
Silver Wolves: The Mad Hatters Mixed-up Objects
Task: Identify a simple object viewed from the side and the top.
"Oh no, Cubs! The Mad Hatter hosted a chaotic tea party, and Wonderland is
completely topsy-turvy! All of his favorite belongings have been mixed up, filpped
upside down, and spun around. Some are seen from the side, and some are seen
from the top! The Hatter needs the clever Silver Wolves to use their eagle eyes and
sharp memories to match the objects up and restore order before the Queen of
Hearts arrives!"
The Setup
1. Divide the Silver Wolves into two equal teams and have them stand in two
parallel lines facing the playing area.
2. Shufefl all 20 cards (10 matching pairs).
3. Lay the cards out face down on the fol or in a neat grid (e.g., 4 rows of 5
cards).
How to Play
1. Team 1 goes frist. One designated player from Team 1 runs up and filps over
any card to reveal the object.
2. That same player filps over a second card, trying to fni d its matching
perspective (e.g., matching the side-view teacup with the top-view teacup).
3. If it’s a match: The player takes both cards back to their team’s pile. Team 1
scores a point.
4. If it’s NOT a match: The player filps both cards face down exactly where they
found them. Turn passes to Team 2.
5. The game continues back and forth until all 10 pairs have been collected.
6. The team with the most matching pairs wins!
The objects cards are:
1. Tea cup
2. Top hat
3. Key
4. Rose
5. Bottle
6. Cake
7. Mushroom
8. Pocket watch
9. Flamingo
10. Playing Card

group.

found them. Turn passes to Team 2.
5. The game continues back and forth until all 10 pairs have been collected.

All my friends are hiding in difefrent rooms of the Wonderland House, and I can’t
remember where everyone is.
Could you help me by drawing a map of the house? Then I can use your map to
fni d the Mad Hatter, the White Rabbit and all my new Wonderland friends.
There’s just one thing you need to remember . . . I need a map that shows what the
house looks like when you look down at it from the sky, like a bird fyling overhead.
Will you help me?”

pencil.

parts of the hall, grounds, den, frie pit, etc. i.e. The Wonderland house &

- Name the rooms - write the names or the characters or draw their

- Which room is next to the Mad Hatters tea room?
- Which room would Alice pass through to reach the White Rabbit?

room?

WYVALJA DPSKSPML AYLLZ HUK MSVDLYZ RLLW YVHKZ HUK ILHJOLZ MYLL VM

Leader's answer: PROTECT WILDLIFE TREES AND FLOWERS KEEP ROADS AND

Challenge 2 and 3: Find Your Way Through the Queen's Maze (+/-20 min)
Now that you have deciphered the code the palace doors are open, but you are
trapped in the courtyard!
At this base split the GW’s into two groups - half do knots, half do compass and
then swap
● Show how to use use a compass and care for it
How to use a compass
1. Hold the compass fal t in the palm of your hand.
2. Keep it away from metal objects and electronic devices.
3. Allow the needle to settle.
4. Identify the north-seeking end of the needle (usually red).
5. Turn the compass housing until the N marking lines up with the
north-seeking needle.
6. Identify North, South, East and West.
How to care for a compass
● Don't drop or throw it.
● Keep it away from magnets and strong magnetic fields.
● Keep it clean and dry.
● Store it safely when not in use.
● Don't leave it in extreme heat.
● Use a compass and one other outdoor method to find North.
● Other methods to find North - Analogue clock and Shadow Stick
https://scoutwiki.scouts.org.za/wiki/Finding_North_and_South
● Tie the following knot - Sheepshank
Challenge 4: The Final Escape- Cross the Queen's Road (+/-7 min)
Beware of the Royal Trafcfi ! Now that you have escaped the courtyard you discover
a busy road filled with the Queens' playing-card soldiers.
● Correctly identify and explain 6–10 road signs to find a safe way across.
● Working in pairs each pair gets a sheet with the names of road signs on -
they must wander the courtyard looking for road signs and writing the

Ice breaker GAME: 
Directions
Have the group stand in the circle.
Everyone must reach in with both of their hands and grab somebody else’s hand. They must be holding hands with two different people. This creates the “human knot”.
Now, everyone must work together to untie the knot without letting go of any hands. They will need to step over or duck under each other.
In the end they will be untied into on large circle or sometimes two small circles.
Notes
Occasionally you get a combination which makes it impossible to completely untie the knot. In this case, the group leader can direct the knot to break at one point, untangle a little, and then reconnect

records.activity:
What Went Wrong?” Investigation
“You’ve arrived at the polluted river. Your job as Water Rescuers is
to figure out what caused the damage.”
Teach 3 Causes:
1. Littering – plastics and rubbish
• A plastic bottle can take over 400 years to break down!
• Many animals think plastic is food and can get very sick or
even die from eating it.
• Rain can wash litter from streets straight into rivers and the
ocean.
• Even small items like sweet wrappers can harm fish and birds.
• If rubbish is left on the ground, it almost always ends up in
water eventually.
“If it’s on the ground, it can reach the water!”
2. Chemicals & Factory Waste
• Some factories release dirty or toxic water into rivers if not
controlled.
• Oil spills can cover water and stop fish and plants from getting
oxygen.
• Chemicals in water can make animals sick—even if the water
looks clean.
• Soap, cleaning products, and paint washed down drains can
harm rivers.
• Once chemicals are in the water, they can be very hard to
remove.
“Not all pollution can be seen—clear water is not always clean!”
3. Runoff – Rain Washing Dirt & Chemicals
• When it rains, water washes everything on the ground into
drains and rivers.
• Fertilisers from gardens or farms can cause too much plant
growth in water, which can kill fish.
• Soap from washing cars or pavements can pollute rivers.
• Oil from roads can be washed into stormwater systems.
• Stormwater drains often go directly to rivers or the ocean—
without cleaning the water first.

records.activity:
Step 1: Prepare the Bottle
• Turn the top half of the bottle upside down (like a funnel)
• Place it into the bottom half or into a cup
Explain: “This will act like our filter system.”
Step 2: Add the First Layer (Cloth/Cotton)
• Place cloth, cotton wool, or a coffee filter at the bottom
(the bottle neck)
Explain:
“This layer stops the smallest dirt from passing through.”
Step 3: Add Sand Layer
• Pour in a layer of fine sand
Explain:
“Sand catches tiny particles we can’t easily see.”
Step 4: Add Small Stones
• Add a layer of small pebbles or gravel
Explain:
“These trap bigger bits of dirt and debris.”
Step 5: Add Larger Stones (Top Layer)
• Add larger stones at the top
Explain:
“This helps catch large pieces like leaves and litter first.”
Step 6: Pour Dirty Water Slowly
• Carefully pour dirty water into the top
Important:
Go slowly to avoid mixing the layers
Step 7: Watch the Water Drip Through
• Observe as water filters into the container
Ask Cubs:
• “Is it clearer?”
• “What changed?”
Always say: “This water may look cleaner, but it is NOT safe to
drink.”
Discussion Questions
• Which layer worked the best?
• What got trapped at the top vs bottom?
• Is it easy or hard to clean water?

The Acid Rain Investigation”
“Acid rain is rain that has been polluted by dirty air. When smoke
and gases from cars and factories go into the sky, they mix with
clouds and turn into acid rain.”
• Acid rain is caused by air pollution (cars, factories,
burning fuels)
• It falls as rain, mist, or even snow
• It can harm plants, animals, rivers, and buildings
• It can make water in rivers too acidic for fish to survive
• It can damage forests by burning leaves and weakening
trees
“Dirty air can turn into harmful rain!”

records.activity:
Kim’s Game: Memory and Observation
(Explain what a Kim’s game is)
A Kim’s game is a memory and observation game that
scouts play to develop their capacity to observe and
remember details. The game is named after Rudyard
Kipling’s character,Kim, who trains to be a spy by
memorizing objects. It helps scouts learn to focus and
concentrate on details.
1. Set up: Gather 10 -20 items (Small/Everyday kind of
items). place them on a tray or flat surface.
2. Observe: Give cubs a minute to memorize the items and
their positions.
3. Hide: Cover the tray with a cloth,towel or blanket.
4. Memorize: Cubs to draw or write down what they saw.
5. Remove items and repeat it again. Cubs to spot what
items were missing.

records.activity:
Marble Run, & Cross the River.
2 teams, each given an A4 card per person. One
marble per team. Team lines up, curls their cards, and
the player at the back starts rolling the marble along
the card (without touching it. The player in front of that
player has their card ready to take the marble and roll it
to the player in front of them. The first player must run
to the front of the line, ready to get the marble when it
arrives. This continues, without touching the marble,
until the marble is by the mug. The marble must land
in the mug. If the marble falls off during the game, the
team must start again.
Once the marble is in the mug, the team must cross a
space (river) without touching the floor (water). Their
cards are the stepping stones which can be moved.
records.title: Marble Run, & Cross the River.

records.activity:
Obstacle Race Puzzle
Two teams. Two hoops, upright and off the floor.
Beyond each one, a hoop on the ground with golf balls
inside. Also beyond the hoops, orange cones in a line.
In front of the hoops a spoon, with a long handle, on
the ground. Bags beyond the cones, each with a puzzle
piece inside. Teams each have a board with them to
build the puzzle on.
One team member is the puzzle builder. Others do the
obstacle course as follows. Run to the hoops, pick up
the spoon, reach through the hoop to get a ball on the
spoon, bring the ball back through the hoop. Put the
ball on the ground and dribble it with the spoon
around the hoops and cones. Pick up a bag and dribble
the ball back to the hoop on the ground. Put the ball in
the hoop and run back to the puzzle builder with the
bag. The next player in the team then repeats the
procedure until all puzzle pieces have been collected.
The winning team finishes the puzzle first.

records.activity:
Lets play Mancala!
Mancala is one of the oldest board games in the world, with origins
traced back to ancient Africa.
Setup & Mechanics
● Board Setup: 12 small pits (6 per player) and 2 large end
stores (Mancalas). Place 4 beans in each of the 12 pits (48
total).
● Objective: Capture and store more beans in your store than
your opponent.
Core Rules
● Sowing: On your turn, pick up all beans from any pit on your
side and deposit them one by one counterclockwise into
adjacent pits, including your store (skip your opponent's store).
● Free Turn: If your last dropped seed lands directly in your own
store, you get an immediate extra turn.
● Capturing: If your last dropped seed lands in an empty pit on
your side, you capture that seed along with all beans in the
opponent's pit directly opposite, placing them into your store.
● Game End: The game ends as soon as one player's 6 pits are
completely empty. The other player gathers all remaining
beans on their side and puts them in their store. The player
with the most total beans wins
games

safely into the cave, they run back to their team and the next

team to save all the Bambi’s is the winner.

records.activity:
Team Game - Water carrying
Divide the Pack into two teams. Place a bucket of water in
front of each team and an empty bucket at the back. Cubs to
sit in a line about an arms-length apart. The front Cub is given
a mug. At ‘go’ he/she dips the mug into the water and passes
it to the net Cub and so on down to the end of the line. When
the last Cub receives it he/she pours the water into the empty
bucket and the empty mug is then passed back up the line.
The first cub again fills the mug and passes it down and so on
until the mug has been filled five times in all. The cubs should
try not to spill. At the end of the game the Leader should
measure the water level in each bucket and award bones
accordingly.

records.activity:
Sense Game (Sound) – Rub A Dub – Dub
You will need 20 (or more) film canisters or similar; these
should be opaque and all look the same. Into half of these you
place a marble, bell, or anything that will make a noise when
the container is shaken. The Cubs sit in a circle and take it in
turn to pick up two containers at a time and give them a shake.
If they both rattle then a point is given to the Cub who picked
them up. These containers are then removed from the game
and the next Cub has a turn. If both containers don’t rattle then
they are both replaced where they were picked up from and
the game continues. The game gets more difficult as more and
more containers are removed as there are more empty ones
left in the game than ones that rattle. This game can also be
played as a team with the winning team being the one with the
most points.

ACTIVE GAME: Reach and rescue
Cubs line up, back-to-back, in two equal lines down the centre of the playing area. Demarcate the boundaries if playing outdoors. One team are ‘reaches’ and the other team ‘rescuers’. The leader calls out rrrreaches or rrrrescuers (rolling the ‘r’ so that the Cubs cannot guess what is coming). If ‘rescuers’ is called, they turn and chase the ‘reaches’. Any ‘reaches’ caught join the ‘rescuers’ team. The ‘reachers’ who cross the designated boundary line cannot be caught. The game continues. When time is up, the largest team is the winner.

ACTIVITY: EmergenciesThe Gold Wolf Aptitude challenge requirement is to ‘know how to behave in an emergency situation’ but do our Cubs know what an emergency is? Use this link to get the local emergency numbers emailed to you for your area: https://safemynumber.co.za/
Have they ever experienced an emergency?
What are they going to do in an emergency?
Which number do they phone in an emergency -there are various emergency services when you dial 112 (ambulance, fire and rescue, NSRI, etc.)?
The Cubs should be reminded that even though, an emergency is scary, they need to speak as calmly as possible. Make sure that the Cubs understand that calling 112 as a joke is a crime. Stress that whenever an unnecessary call is made to 112, it can delay a response to someone who needs it. Go through some of the questions the 112 operators will ask (see below).
Teach the Cubs the 112 song. Left finger up (one); right finger up (one); bring the left and right fingers together to form a 2 … 112.

ACTIVE GAME: Float or sink
Cubs stand in the middle of the playing area. Label one of the ends as ‘floating’ and the other as ‘sinking’. The Cubs must listen to the objects being called out and then have to run to that end of the playing area. The last one there must tell you a water safety rule before they can re-join the game.
Objects that sink: Rocks; stones; marbles; coins; keys
Objects that float: Apples; wood; empty plastic bottle; ball; inflated balloon; boat

records.activity:
DEMONSTRATION: Recovery position
The first thing to do, without delay, is to lay the victim on their side, open the airway and keep it open. If the head is tilted forwards this may obstruct the airway and hinder breathing, so tilt the person’s head back as far as it can go. Very often breathing will start again quite naturally. A person who cannot breathe naturally willstruggle for breath, and their face and lips will turn blue. 
As soon as natural breathing starts, the heaving movements of the chest will stop, and the colour of the face and lips will turn pink again.
Allow the Cubs to practise putting each other in the recovery positions.
records.title: DEMONSTRATION: Recovery position

records.activity:
SENSE TRAINING (Touch): Hidden hazards
In a large flat-ish bucket, place about 30cm of water. 
Put in several marbles. Cubs, in teams, need to “fish” out the marbles or small stones using only their toes!
The team to fish out the most marbles is the winner. 
To add an extra fun element, add dishwashing liquid to create bubbles.

Game: Stuck in the mud
Aim: Don’t get caught and become “stuck in the mud”!
Choose 2-3 players to be the catchers (“the mud”).
Everyone else runs around inside the playing area.
If a catcher tags you, you are stuck in the mud.
When stuck, stand still with your legs apart and call, “Help me!”
Other players can rescue you by crawling underneath your legs.
Once someone goes underneath your legs, you are free and can run again.
No pushing, pulling, or tackling.
Players must stay inside the marked playing area.
The game ends when everyone is stuck, or after a set time.
Choose new catchers and play again!

Instructions: How to Play:
Form a Circle: All players stand in a circle facing inward.
First Round: Pair up with the person next to you and play a standard game of Rock-Paper-Scissors.
The loser steps behind the winner and places their hands on the winner's shoulders to start a "train."
Build the Trains: Each train leader (the player at the front) finds another leader to play Rock-Paper-Scissors against.
The losing leader and their entire train join the back of the winning leader's train.
Winning the Game: Continue playing until every player has joined one massive train behind the final winner!

The Game: The Six forms a single line. Each member takes a turn reaching inside the container to identify the 6 mystery items.

The Game: The Six sits in a circle, listens to the songs, and works together to recall and guess the exact order in which the songs were played.

WIDE GAME: Cub Red Light, Green Light
Instructions: Game Setup
Starting Line: The Cubs line up about 300 meters away from the Game Instructor.
Instructor's Position: The Game Instructor stands with their back turned toward the Cubs.
Objective: The first Cub (or Cubs) to cross the finish line wins!

Game Commands & Actions
While the Instructor's back is turned, the Cubs move forward toward the finish line. When the Instructor calls out a command and turns around, the Cubs must instantly perform the correct action:
"Cub Salute" Cubs must immediately stop and salute.
Note: Any Cub caught still moving when the Instructor turns around must return to the starting line.
"Grand Howl" Cubs must quickly form a circle.
"Promise" Cubs must stop and salute using their right hand.
"Old Wolf" Cubs must point to an Old Wolf (a Cub Leader).
"Left Handshake" Cubs must quickly find a partner and shake hands using their left hand.

Playing
Setup & Knotwork: Divide the Pack into pairs. Each pair ties themselves together at opposite ends of a rope using either a Slip Reef Knot (Silver Wolf) or a Bowline (Gold Wolf).

Winning Condition: When the whistle blows, the team with the most uncaught Cubs wins! 
Pack-Up: After the game, every pair must properly hank their rope and return it to equipment storage.

ACTIVE GAME: Eco-Ranger Challenge: The Ultimate Wildlife Relay
Game Setup
Teams: 3 teams of 6 players (1 runner per team at a time).
Equipment Needed: Ropes, open-ended crawling barrels, sticks, "Journey of a Raindrop" worksheets, and "South African Endangered Animals" charts.
Course Layout
Start Line: Team queuing area supplied with skipping ropes.
Halfway Station: Open-ended crawling barrel with the "Journey of a Raindrop" worksheet setup.
Finish Line: Wooden stick frame holding the "South African Endangered Animals" worksheet.
Player Gameplay Routine
Leg 1: Jump rope from the Start Line to the Halfway Station, crawl completely through the barrel, and fill in 1 step of the 5-step "Journey of a Raindrop" worksheet (Player 6 verifies and approves all 5 steps).
Leg 2: Pick up a stick, balance it horizontally on one hand while running from the Halfway Station to the Finish Line, and mark 1 correct threat for an assigned animal on the chart.
Leg 3: Sprint directly back to the Start Line and tag the next teammate.
Winning Condition The first team to have all 6 players complete the course with both worksheets fully and accurately completed wins!
Bones:
1st Place: 3 Bones
2nd Place: 2 Bones
3rd Place: 1 Bones

records.activity:
Active Game: Resource Dash: The Natural Element Challenge
How to Play:
Kids line up at the start line in two lines behind each other.
The leader calls out an item that depends on one of those natural resources:
"River / Fish / Rain" Move LEFT (Water)
"Vegetables / Crops / Worms" Move RIGHT (Soil/Land)
Paper / Apples / Wood" Move MIDDLE (Trees & Forests)
Man-made Items (e.g., Plastic, Metal) FREEZE / STAND STILL (or FREEZE / STAND STILL if an item needs no resource, like plastic or metal).
Any player who moves in the wrong direction or fails to freeze when required goes back 2 steps! First group with all players to reach the end wins.

Activity: Seed Hunt & Conservation Challenge

Instructions
Base 1: Seed Hunt & Sprouting Jar:
Provide Cubs with a glass bottle to use as a water scope to retrieve the soaked seeds.
Have Cubs transfer their seeds in a plastic pocket lined with damp cotton wool to take home and watch grow.
Base 2: Compost Collection:
Ask everyone to deposit all organic waste and compostable materials into a shared bucket.
Explain that this will be turned into rich compost to feed their sprouted seeds once they are transplanted.
Base 3: Home Energy Audit (Discussion):
Gather the Cubs to identify everyday household activities that waste or consume electricity and energy.
Discuss practical steps they can take at home to conserve energy (e.g., turning off lights, unplugging unused chargers, keeping fridge doors closed, switching to cold water washes).

RELAY GAME: Tins game: Drie Blikkies, Dithini, Amathini, or Tin Bati

1. Knock 'Em Down: Break the tower to start.
Line up 5 steps away from the stacked cans. A Builder throws the ball to knock down the 3 cans. You get 3 tries!
2. Get the Ball:Run and dodge!.
As soon as the cans fall, the Catchers run to grab the ball. The Builders run in to fix the cans!
3. Build and Dodge:Fast hands and quick feet.
Builders try to stack all 3 cans back up. Catchers throw the ball at the Builders to tap them OUT (below the waist only!). Catchers can pass the ball to each other to get closer.
4. Win the Point!: How to win the round.
Builders Win: If you stack all 3 cans and shout " Drie Blikkies, Dithini, Amathini,!" before anyone gets hit, you get 1 point!
Catchers Win: If the Catchers hit a Builder with the ball, that Builder is out. Hit all Builders to swap sides!

2nd Place: 2 Bones

records.activity:
Activity: The Great Hazard Hunt

Instructions for Cubs:
Inspect the Scene: Lay out the Safety Problem visual. Look closely at the pictures to spot the household dangers, street risks, and internet safety problems.
Match the Rules: Read your Safety Rule cards together and use your Pritt Stick to paste each card next to its matching problem on the sheet:
Rule A (Home Safety): Pick up messy toys and stay clear of household chemicals to stop trips and poison risks.
Rule B (Pedestrian Safety): Always wait for the green light, look both ways, and cross strictly at marked crosswalks.
Rule C (Stranger Danger): Stay alert—never accept gifts or talk to strangers, and step away if approached.
Rule D (Unsafe Situations): If someone follows you or makes you feel uncomfortable, run away immediately to a public place and tell a trusted adult.
Rule E (Home Alone Safety): Keep doors locked, do not answer the door or phone for strangers, and stick to safe activities like reading.
Scouter Inspection: Shouting "Safety Clear!" alerts Akela to check your matches. Earn 1 point per correct match, with a 2-point speed bonus for the first team to correctly link all 5 safety hazards!

 1 Safety Problem Visual Sheet per Six
 1 Set of Safety Rule Cards (A, B, C, D, E)
 Pritt Stick

records.activity:
Traditional Dance off Game: The Great South African Groove-Off
How to Play
Split into Two Teams: We are dividing the pack into two awesome teams.
Team Huddle (Brainstorming Time): Work with your team to pick 3 traditional dances that you know or want to perform—like the Gumboot dance, the Riel dance, Volkspele, Bhangra, or an English Barn dance!
The 3-Minute Dance Battle: When the music hits, each team gets 3 full minutes per dance to show off their best moves, sync up, and keep the energy super high on the dance floor!
After the dance each cub group must list the groups their dances belong to and each cub must choose one group and share something interesting about their chosen culture with the Pack.
How to Win:
Teamwork: Everyone stays on the dance floor together for all 3 minutes.
Rhythm & Energy: Keep stomping, clapping, spinning, and moving until the music stops!
Creativity: Bring out those big smiles and awesome cultural dance moves!

records.activity:
Activity: The Great Flag Recall Challenge
How it Works:
The Study Phase (Look & Learn):
Show the cubs the visual flag diagram with all parts labeled (Toggle, Fly, Hoist, Breadth/Width, Rope, and Length).
Give each Six 60 seconds to study the diagram, memorize the locations, and plan their strategy together.
The Memory Sprint:
Hide the diagram!
Hand each Six a stack of 6 unplaced label cards and a strip of blue-tack/tape.
On the whistle, the cubs race over to their physical Pack flag laid flat on the ground or table.
Labeling the Flag:
Working completely from memory, team members must place each label on its matching part:
Toggle: The small wooden/plastic pin near the top.
Fly: The outer edge that waves in the wind.
Hoist: The vertical edge closest to the rope/pole.
Breadth / Width: The top-to-bottom height line of the flag.
Rope: The line (halyard) used to pull the flag up.
Length: The front-to-back horizontal measurement of the flag.
Scouter Inspection:
Once all 6 labels are stuck down, the Sixer shouts "Flag Complete!"
Scouters check the placements. Award 1 point per correct label, plus a 2-point speed bonus for the first Six to get all 6 parts 100% correct!
records.equipment:
1 Physical Pack Flag (laid flat on a table or grass)

1 Set of Label Cards: Toggle, Fly, Hoist, Breadth/Width, Rope, and Length

Pristik (to stick labels onto the flag)

For the Bottle Method: Pierce a small hole in the cap of
the plastic bottle. Place the top half of the bottle inside

Game : Drop the Hankerchief
For this traditional Egyptian game, two teams of 5
players or more gather plus one leader. Each person
from the teams call out numbers, 1 through 5. The
leader holds a handkerchief up between the two teams
and yells out a number; the players from both teams
that have that number run and try to catch the
handkerchief before it falls to the ground. If you can
catch it first, you get a point, but only if you can make it
back to your side without the opposite team tagging
you.

records.activity:
Crafts : Walls of the Pharoah's Tomb
The Egyptian hieroglyphics alphabet consists of 24
single-consonant signs that function similarly to modern
letters, forming the phonetic basis of the writing
system.
Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs were a formal writing
system used for over 3,500 years, combining
ideographic, logographic, syllabic, and alphabetic
elements with more than 1,000 distinct
characters. While many hieroglyphs represented entire
words or concepts (ideograms), a subset of 24 symbols
represented single consonant sounds, forming the
Egyptian phonetic alphabet. Vowels were generally not
written, so the alphabet focused on consonant sounds,
similar to early Semitic scripts.
Hieroglyphs could be written in multiple directions: left
to right, right to left, top to bottom, or even in circular
arrangements. The direction was determined by the
orientation of the symbols, particularly those depicting
living creatures, which faced the beginning of the line.
There was no punctuation, and symbols could serve as
ideograms (whole words) or phonograms (sounds or
parts of words), making the system complex to learn
and interpret.
Hieroglyphic writing was primarily used by priests and
scribes, with only about 1% of the population able to
read it. It appeared around 3200 BCE and evolved into
cursive forms like hieratic and later demotic scripts for
practical purposes. The script was considered sacred,
often associated with the god Thoth, and was used
extensively in temples, tombs, and religious texts.

Drill a hole through both ends of the PVC piping, making
sure to keep it straight and that it comes through the
other side.
Tie the string through the first hole and knot it tightly.
Then pull it very taught (ask someone to help) and then
tie it through the inside hole on the other end. The bow
should be bent into an arc shape and the string needs
to be as taught as possible. (The string on ours
measures 74 cm when taught,)
Because of the strength of the materials, the bow will
retain its shape and stay strong and tight.
To make the arrow, add a little piece of folded felt (or
newspaper/ cloth) at the end of the bamboo cane, then
wrap over the top of it with duct tape to keep it in
place.
Cut some large oval type shapes from felt and wrap one
over the end of each arrow, keeping them firmly in pace
by fixing them around the middle with an elastic band.
On the opposite end, cut a small notch into the wood,
right in the centre, using a small saw, so that the bow
can be pulled back into the string to line it up.
That’s all there is to the arrows! The ends should feel

records.activity:
Activities : Machine Challenge
Cubs to complete the various challenges. They can
divide into smaller groups if needed and do each
challenge separately.
Lever – Lift the Load
Place a heavy box or bucket on the floor. Give Cubs a
broomstick and a wooden block as the fulcrum. They
have to lift the load without picking it up. Move the
fulcrum closer to and farther from the load so they
discover that its position changes how much effort is
needed.
Key idea: A lever lets us move a heavy load using less
effort.
Examples: seesaw, bottle opener, crowbar, scissors.
Pulley – Rescue the Supplies
Run rope through a pulley or over a pole attached to
something secure or even a tree branch. Cubs lift a
bucket containing beanbags or another small weight. If
possible, let them first lift the bucket directly and then
with the pulley.
Key idea: A pulley changes the direction of the force
and can make lifting easier.
Inclined Plane – Mountain Supply Run
Place one end of a plank on a chair or sturdy box. Cubs
race cars down the ramp. Change the angle to see
what effect it has (cars go faster/further if incline is
higher).
Key idea: A ramp lets us use less force over a longer
distance.
Examples: wheelchair ramp, stairs, loading ramp, slide.
Screw – Up We Go
Give each Cub a large bolt and nut. Race to see who
can move the nut from one end to the other. Then show
that the thread is essentially an inclined plane wrapped
around a cylinder. If you have wood and appropriate
supervision, Cubs can also drive a screw into soft wood
with a screwdriver. The nut and bolts can be done as a
relay race.

who are closest to the bean bag

squeezed, they grab the bean bag.

records.activity:
DEMONSTRATION:
Have two Cubs step up to the front. Have one stand on
a step or something higher, and the other standing
opposite on the ground. Use this time to demonstrate
one child needing assistance in the water (the one on
the ground) and the other helping from the shore/bank
(the one on the step). The Cub ‘in the water’ then pulls
the other slowly off the step and they are now both ‘in
the water’. Explain that the step is the bank of the
river/lake/dam and when you try to help with your hand
you have very little balance and are at risk of falling into
the water. Highlight that the drowning Cub (victim) will
use all their strength to stay above water and
unintentionally push the other (the Cub that was pulled
off the shore) underwater.
Fear will set in for the second Cub, and they react in the
same manner thus pushing the first Cub back under
water. This see-saw action will continue until one Cub
can no longer get back above water and it's at this point
that one or both will drown.

This year we have been focusing on books and stories. Some stories are fictional –
meaning they are made up and some stories are non-fiction which mean they are real or
based on facts. Tonight’s book or story is The Snail Trail. Snails are interesting little
creatures with soft bodies and a hard shell. They don’t have any legs, but they do have a
foot. Let’s inspect our feet (shoes).
Inspection: Shoes
Did you know snails and slugs both belong to the same family? They are both
Gastropods. Snails have a hard shell but slugs have no shells.
Snails can be found all over the world both on land and water. They are found in the sea
and fresh water. The largest snail is the Giant African Snail. He can be up to 35cm long
and weigh over 2 kg. Think how heavy it must be for him to drag his shell around with
him. How heavy are you?

Every good story begins with a setting. Tonight our story begins beside a peaceful little river. But rivers do not always stay peaceful...
The Cubs in our story have reached high ground. Looking down into the valley, they see a little village below. What will happen when
all that water reaches it?

WATER BREAK
Quick drink and toilet break. Use the buddy system.
The villagers survived their first storm, but their story is not finished. They now know what went wrong - and another storm is
coming. Refreshed and ready, they have a chance to change the ending.
We cannot always stand beside someone to warn them when water becomes dangerous. Sometimes the best way to keep people
safe is to share what we know - especially with younger children.
Our Cubs have built a village, watched a disaster happen, rebuilt it and found a way to warn other people. Before we pass the story
on, there is one more story to hear.
Every story leaves us with something to remember. Tonight the river reminds us that we cannot always stop water, but we can
recognise danger, prepare and help other people stay safe. Now it is your turn to pass the story on.
Tonight our Sixes have become builders, problem-solvers and storytellers. The village survived because people learnt from
what happened - and now you can use your story to help somebody else stay safe around water. Now it is time to join the
Scouts and carry our stories to the campfire.
• Flood in a Tray: Cubs build and flood their landscape, observe the effects, make improvements and test it again.

records.activity:
Listen Like an Owl
Prepare short recordings of these three distinctive bird calls:
1. Hadeda ibis
2. Laughing dove
3. Grey go-away-bird
Play each recording loudly enough for the whole Pack to
hear, but keep the phone screen hidden.
Instructions
1. Gather the Cubs quietly and ask them to close their
eyes.
2. Introduce each bird by playing its call and then revealing
its name and picture.
3. Replay all three calls in a different order.
4. Cubs raise their hands when they recognise a call.
5. The first Cub to identify it correctly earns a bone for
their Six.
6. Finish with a memory round by playing all three calls
consecutively. The first Six to give the complete correct
order earns a bonus bone.
Remind the Cubs that they must listen silently until the
recording has finished and may make only one guess per
call.

records.activity:
Game: Birds Fly
1. Cubs spread out facing the leader.
2. The leader calls the name of an animal while flapping
their arms and saying, for example, “Hadedas fly!”
3. If the named animal can fly, the Cubs flap their wings.
4. If it cannot fly, they must remain completely still—even
if the leader flaps.
5. A Cub who moves incorrectly performs a fun action,
such as three “chick hops”, before rejoining.
6. Gradually increase the speed and mix birds with animals
such as bats, butterflies, elephants, penguins and
ostriches.
7. Allow individual Cubs to take turns as the caller.

remember which birds are flightless.

records.activity:
Game: Rangers and Raiders
This is a Wild Side version of Rats and Rabbits.
Divide the Cubs into two equal teams: Rangers and Raiders.
The teams stand in two lines, back-to-back, about one metre
apart. Mark a safe line approximately ten metres in front of
each team.
The leader calls either “Rrrrrangers!” or “Rrrrraiders!” If
Rangers are called, they turn and chase the Raiders towards
the Raiders’ safe line. If Raiders are called, they chase the
Rangers. Anyone tagged before reaching safety joins the
opposing team.
Use a long “Rrrrr…” before completing the name to build
suspense. Cubs may tag only with an open hand—no
pushing, grabbing clothing or diving.

The Unnatural Trail
Place 12–15 everyday objects along a short outdoor trail.
Some should be obvious, while others should be partly
concealed among plants, rocks or trees. Cubs walk the trail
silently in small groups and count how many unnatural
objects they can spot. They must not point at, touch or
reveal the objects to others. At the end, each group quietly
reports its total and describes what it saw. Walk the trail
together afterwards to reveal the objects.

Give each Six five minutes to collect only loose natural
materials already lying on the ground, such as leaves, grass,
twigs, stones and seed pods. They then use these materials
to create a wild animal on the ground. Nothing may be
picked from a living plant.
Each Six has one minute to introduce its creature, give it a
name and explain:
• Where it lives
• What it eats
• How it protects itself
• Why its habitat should be protected
Finish by returning the materials to nature and leaving the
area tidy.

Each six is given an oversized T-shirt. The first cub in line puts on the T-Shirt. They turn and face the second player in their team's line.The first and second players both hold each others hands. Then when you say GO, the rest of the team in their line pulls the shirt up and over the first players head, down the first player's arms and up the arms of the second player and over the second player's body (the shirt will be inside out at this point).Then the second player turns and faces the third player and the team repeats the process. They continue this all the way down their team's line until the last player is wearing the T-shirt. The team to transfer the T-shirt through their whole team first wins.

Players sit in a circle and start counting round the circle from "one." If the agreed figure for the game is seven, each time the number being called includes the figure seven or is a multiple of seven, the player keeps quiet and clasps his hands together. If anyone makes a mistake the leader records a point against him.
When the boys become good at this game, add one or two other numbers, so they will have to keep very sharp not to get caught with numbers four, six and eight going on at once.
For one number the player clasps hands. For the second number he will put both hands above his head. For the third number he can nod his head. Most players will find thinking of two numbers at once difficult enough.

Activity 1: Steam Release – Mr. Wolf
Choose one cub to be the wolf. The wolf stands at one
end of the room or field, with their back facing the other
cubs. The other cubs line up at the opposite end of the
play area.
The other cubs call out in unison: "What's the time, Mr.
Wolf?" The wolf turns around and yells a time, such as
"It's 3 o'clock!" The cubs take that same number of steps
forward (three steps, in this example). The cubs keep
moving closer to the wolf with each new time.
When the cubs get very close, the wolf can shout: "It's
dinner time!" Instead of giving a time, the wolf turns
around and chases the cubs. The cubs run back to the
starting line to stay safe.
If the wolf tags a cub before they reach safety, that
tagged cub becomes the new wolf for the next round.

Activity 9: Drip, Drip Splash
Similar to Duck-Duck-Goose
• Cubs to sit in a circle
• Assign "It": One player stands up with a small sponge
soaked in water or a cup filled with water.
• "It" walks around the outside of the circle, lightly
trickling or tapping a tiny bit of water onto each
player's head and saying "Drip".
• When "It" chooses a target, they pour or dump the rest
of the water onto that person's head and shout
"Splash" (or "Drop" / "Drench").
• The splashed player jumps up and chases "It" once
around the circle. "It" tries to run all the way around
and sit in the empty spot before getting tagged.
• Next round: If "It" is caught, they go again. If "It" makes
it to the empty seat safely, the splashed player
becomes the new "It".

records.title:
Game/ Activity: STEAM
REALEASE: Weeds
and Wegetables
records.activity:
Instructions:  Divide your group into two equal teams.
 Have the teams form two parallel lines facing each other, about 1 meter apart.
 Designate one line as the Weeds and the other as the Wegetables so that every
player has a partner opposite them.
 Mark two parallel safety lines (baselines) about 10–20 meters away from the center,
one behind the Rats and one behind the Rabbits.
 The leader/coach shouts either "Weeds" or "Wegetables".
 If "Weeds" is called, the Weeds must turn and sprint to their safety line before their
Wegetable partner can tag them on the waist or back.
 If "Wegetables" is called, the roles reverse; the Wegetables sprint to their safety line
while the weeds give chase.
 Players score a point if they successfully reach the line without being tagged, or if they
tag their partner before they reach the safe zone.
To make the game harder or more engaging for older kids, try starting from different
positions instead of standing up: [1]
• Back-to-back: Players start sitting or standing back-to-back.
• Plank position: Players start in a push-up/plank position facing away from each
other.
• Belly-down: Players lie flat on their stomachs with their feet touching the center
line.

records.activity:
Ladders

Detailed source attachment:
Instructions: Players split into pairs of equal size or ability.
Pairs sit on the floor facing each other in two long parallel lines with their legs
stretched straight out, touching feet with their partner. The gaps between each
pair's legs form the "rungs" of the ladder.
Each pair is given a number
The leader stands at one end of the room and calls out a number:
Both players in that pair stand up as quickly as possible.
They run down the middle of the "ladder," carefully stepping over the legs of
the other sitting pairs.
When they reach the far end of the ladder, they run around the outside of the
sitting players, heading back toward the opposite end.
They enter the middle of the ladder again from the other end and race back to
their original spot.
The first runner to sit back down in their original spot with their legs stretched out
earns a point for their team

Dottie McStuffins, known as Doc to her friends, is a doctor to her toys. Tonight Doc has a new kind of case:
keeping her toys safe around water. She needs a whole team of Water Heroes - lifeguards, rescue workers,
scientists, first aiders and clever Cubs. Water Heroes wear different uniforms, so let's introduce our Water Hero
team:
Doc's Water Heroes need to react quickly when something goes wrong. Before we can help anyone, we need to
learn the Water Hero emergency commands.
Every doctor and rescue team needs the right equipment. Doc has a medical kit, but tonight she needs a Water
Hero kit. Let's work out what belongs in it and what each item could be used for.
Doc uses clean water to hydrate her patients, clean wounds and cool minor burns. Water Heroes know that clean
water is precious. With your buddy go and have a drink, but don't waste our water.

celebrating one of our own heroes, Tamara, who has worked hard to achieve her Springbok Award.

act. Let's see what you know about being safe in and around water.
